author: NorthEast News Desk
body: North Kingstown-based REGENT has completed the first crewed flight of its Viceroy seaglider prototype on Narragansett Bay, moving the hybrid marine aircraft into the final stage of sea trials.

Two captains were aboard during the test, according to the company. REGENT said the prototype traveled 1,956 feet in ground-effect flight, reaching 33 feet above the water during a 30-second airborne segment.

The craft is designed to operate in three modes: floating from a dock, rising onto hydrofoils and then flying close to the water, where ground effect can reduce aerodynamic drag. REGENT is developing the platform for coastal passenger service, cargo transport and defense missions.

The milestone does not mean the vehicle is ready for commercial passengers. The company said continued testing will focus on refining performance, reducing operational risk and demonstrating readiness for future service. Even so, carrying crew through the full transition from waterborne operation to flight marks a substantial engineering step for a Rhode Island company building a new class of coastal transportation on Narragansett Bay.
dek: The North Kingstown company’s Viceroy prototype carried two captains in a brief ground-effect flight that begins the final stage of sea trials.
headline: REGENT seaglider completes first crewed flight on Narragansett Bay
